refusal_reading.method: Read as text, by searching for each code and reading the lines around every match and every function on the way to it. The bundle was never run, no Collab server was started and no MCP collab tool was called. Line numbers are lines of the bundle, not of the source it was built from.
refusal_reading.rule: A code is listed on an operation only when every place the tool can raise it, called as this adapter calls it (after open, in a bound native session, with no actor argument), comes before the commit of the journal change. A code with one place after a commit is not listed. Whatever is not listed is answered as failed with an unknown effect.
refusal_reading.as_called: After open returned: the tool handlers then take their bound-session branch (the store methods named ...ForSession). The adapter never sends an `actor` argument, and the environment it gives the backend has no session file to resume from (lines 34037 to 34045 read AGENTOOL_COLLAB_SESSION_FILE).
refusal_reading.how_a_refusal_is_answered: Lines 29431 to 29445: every handler runs inside one wrapper that catches any error. An error of the backend's own class becomes {error: <code>, message, ...details} with isError true; anything else becomes internal_error. The answer carries no mark of where it was raised, so a place before a commit and a place after one cannot be told apart from outside.

mutateAsSession.steps: The key is checked (32728). Then one immediate transaction: the session is checked (32730), a receipt for the key is looked up and compared (32733 to 32743), a write-guard row is inserted (32745), the tool's own work runs (32747), the receipt is inserted (32748) and the session is stamped as seen (32754); the guard row is deleted on the way out (32757).

acknowledgeSessionCursor.steps: One immediate transaction (31120 to 31154): the session is checked (31121), the anchor is validated, the cursor version is compared (31137), the cursor row is updated (31144) and the change is counted (31150).
acknowledgeSessionCursor.after_commit: tightenFileModes (31155); then, in the handler, the session's credential file is rewritten (28914)

nextForSession.steps: A first immediate transaction (32403 to 32435) checks the session (32404) and stamps it as seen (32430). Then elapsed handoffs are marked expired in a transaction of their own (32437). Then a second, reading transaction (32438 to 32471) checks the session again (32439).
nextForSession.after_commit: everything from line 32437 on, the second session check among it

getTask.steps: No transaction and no write statement: one SELECT for the task (33414) and one for its artifacts. The handler (28990) does not check the native session.

stages.no_transaction: The tool opens no transaction and runs no write statement on this path.
stages.before_transaction: Raised before the transaction that would change the journal begins.
stages.in_transaction_before_write: Raised inside that transaction, before its first write statement.
stages.in_transaction_after_write: Raised inside that transaction after a write statement it had not committed: the write-guard row (line 32745), and in a few places the row being changed. That nothing of it stays rests on the rollback.
stages.after_commit: Raised after a transaction of this call has committed. A code with such a place is not listed. This word is used in rows that are not listed; the card has no such stage.

table.why_not: The tool checks the session twice. The first check (through line 32404) is the first statement of a transaction that then stamps the session as seen (line 32430) and commits (line 32435). After that the tool reaps elapsed handoffs in a transaction of its own (line 32437), and only then makes the second check (line 32439). A refusal from the second check comes after a commit, and the answer does not say which check raised it.

Both places are before the commit, so the rule would allow it. It is left out because, called as this adapter calls the tool, neither is reached in ordinary running: the first is in a loop over dependencies, and the adapter sends none; the second is a re-read of the row the same transaction has just inserted. An answer with this code would mean the reading is wrong somewhere, so it stays unknown.

refusal_reading.git_before_a_claim: claimTaskForSession (31359) looks up a receipt (31364), then calls captureSessionWorktree (31367), which checks the session (32801) and then inspects the repository (32825): git rev-parse, status, ls-files, diff HEAD, and a digest of untracked file content (lines 29497 to 29600). Only then does the transaction begin (31368). So six of the eight listed codes of task-claim are raised after git ran; idempotency_conflict (at 32720) and session_auth_failed (through 32710 or 32801) can be raised before it. The adapter sets GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 for the backend; what git itself wrote, if anything, was not looked at.

refusal_reading.after_commit_note: These are answered in the same shape as any refusal. It is why the adapter never passes a refusal on by its shape alone, and why a code that is not listed for the operation stays unknown.
stays_unknown: Whether the backend behaves as its text reads. The bundle was never run.

Whether a refused call leaves nothing where it had begun to write. The transaction wrapper is imported from bun:sqlite (line 29451) and is not defined in the bundle; that it rolls back when the function throws is behaviour of the Bun program, which is not pinned.

Whether the reading is complete. It was done once, by the author of this record, following calls by hand from each handler. Nobody read it a second time, and no test can check it: the bundle is not in the repository.

What the MCP library between a handler and the wire does to an answer. Only the handlers' own wrapper (29431 to 29445) was read, and the place where an input the tool's schema refuses is answered with isError and no structuredContent (27688 to 27702).

SQLite itself: a commit that fails, a database that is busy, a trigger that aborts (lines 30298 to 30340). These are not errors of the backend's own class; the wrapper answers them as internal_error, which no card lists.
next: which of its two session checks raised session_auth_failed. It is never passed on.

open: every refusal of collab_session_start. The start runs git, may create or migrate the journal, and commits twice (30781, 30967) before the handler writes the credential file (28820). None of it was read for listing, and the adapter passes none of it on.

Codes that are not candidates of this step, among them dependencies_incomplete, path_scope_conflict, edit_scope_required, worktree_unavailable, worktree_identity_changed, worktree_observation_stale, expected_base_mismatch, cursor_mismatch, cursor_ahead, cursor_fork_detected, cursor_epoch_mismatch, cursor_regression, cursor_recovery_required, session_not_bound, session_workspace_mismatch, workspace_not_found and every invalid_<field>. They were seen on these paths and not read for listing. An answer with one of them is unknown; for a write the binding then sends no more writes.
What git did before a refused claim, and what else the backend's process touched outside the journal.
refusal_reading.what_the_adapter_does_with_it: A listed code is passed on only when the answer also has the plain refusal shape (error and message are strings) and does not carry the key a success carries. The tests show this against the stand-in, which leaves its journal file untouched on a refusal because it was written to. They show nothing about the real backend.

cli_walk.path: As a caller with the door's output only. arrive; explain xenia.covenant; `session` with nothing sent, to read the first line; then one session with six lines: inspect of the operation, an invoke before activation, activate, an invoke with {} (refused), an invoke with no operation (invalid), an invoke with the card's example (returned), end of input. Then the adapter: explain agenttool.collab; a config file in a scratch folder; `session --collab-config <file> --allow` naming open, status and task-get, with seven lines.
core_session: inspect of xenia.covenant draft: the card, allowed true, deadline 10000
invoke before activate: MODULE_INACTIVE, nothing ran, next request activate
invoke with {}: DECLINED invalid_input, not_applied, with the native function's own sentence; next request inspect of the operation
invoke with no operation: INVALID_REQUEST, does_not_match_request, pointer "", keyword required, expected operation
invoke with the example: returned, a draft of 18,741 bytes
end of input: session_end, three modules retired, cleanup complete, exit 0
adapter_session: inspect of agenttool.collab: nine operations, three allowed; look.step not_opened; bound_to shows the scratch paths
invoke task-get with {}: INVALID_INPUT does_not_match_card, pointer "", keyword required, expected task_id; the gate was not asked
invoke task-claim, which the allow list does not name: POLICY_BLOCKED
invoke open: DECLINED bundle_unavailable, because nothing is at the bundle path
end of input: session_end, cleanup complete, exit 0; nothing was created in the scratch folder
cli_walk.a_listed_backend_refusal: Seen once outside the tests, with a scratch script that binds the adapter to the stand-in and runs one session in memory: a claim with a stale version came back DECLINED version_conflict with the card's meaning, and the next claim was admitted. This is the stand-in, not the backend.
still_had_to_guess: Where the pinned bundle comes from. The door says it knows no download. Without those bytes no operation of agenttool.collab can succeed, so the one successful invoke of the walk was on xenia.covenant.
Which Bun to put at bunPath: no version is named, and none is checked.

Which operations to name in --allow before seeing them: the allow list is fixed at the start, and the operations are listed by the first line of a session, by catalog and by explain. A first session without --allow, or a refused start, shows them. It costs a second start.

What operation_started: true means on a refusal the adapter makes before it sends anything (bundle_unavailable, not_open): the handler was entered. The effect, not_applied, and the meaning say that nothing was sent; the field alone reads as if something had begun.

Whether an idempotency key may be used again after a refusal. The card now says what a key is and each next step says to use one not used before, which is always allowed; whether the old one would also be accepted is not said.
What a claim is for when nothing else at this door acts on it: the card says it is a note in the journal, not a lock and not permission. What another session does on seeing it is outside this kit.
How to read `does` and `sites` from inside a session: a session shows an operation's card without them, and they are printed only by explain, at the command line.
no_longer_a_guess: The request forms: all six are on the first line with an example each.
That a module has to be activated: the first line says nothing was activated, and MODULE_INACTIVE gives the request to send.
Which field of a request or an input missed: pointer, keyword and expected name it without repeating what was sent.

mutations: Six single changes were made by hand, one at a time, each restored from a copy afterwards, and the test file for the changed source was run. Each made at least one test fail. They are listed under process_notes. Six is a sample, not a measure of the tests.
not_established: that the adapter works with the real bundle: no test and no command of this step started it, and every Collab test runs a stand-in written in this repository
that the stand-in behaves as the backend does: it was written from a reading of the pinned bundle and never checked against it
that a refusal marked not_applied was observed to change nothing: for the adapter's own refusals it is how the code is written, and for the backend's it is the reading recorded above
that the reading missed no place: a missed one could report a written change as not applied
that Bun or git is a particular program or version, or that Bun rolls a refused transaction back: neither is pinned, and neither was run
that a deadline or a timeout stops code: a deadline ends a wait, and a timeout stops the backend process, not a write it had begun
anything about a caller: who sends requests, whether they may, or what they intend. The gate reads an allow list and nothing else
that the schema checker implements JSON Schema: it reads three types and ten keywords and refuses the rest
that an agent other than the author of this record can follow the door without guessing: the walk was made by the author, who had also read the source
that the two branches named in LINEAGE.md still exist on the remote or are still at those revisions: nothing was fetched
that the totals hold on another machine, on Linux or Windows, or on Node 22
that the hashes describe any later tree, or that the earlier tasks were built test-first as their commits say
that nothing is left behind after a session that opened a real backend: left_behind lists what the binding knows of, and the rest is reported as not surveyed
